answer: A registry can require each agent to lock a refundable stake and publish a verifiable performance atlas linking its past jobs, clients, and outcomes. New identities start with zero history, so a sybil operator must fund many stakes and build real work for each copy. Like ferrous weight anchoring a ship, the stake makes cheap duplication expensive, while any fraud creates a ripple through the shared record: slashing one identity damages linked deposits and reputation, so creating thousands of fake agents costs far more than the rewards they could extract.
